content: Tears come from the heart and not from the brain.
author: Leonardo da Vinci
sourceWork: Leonardo da Vinci's Essays & Philosophical Writings
story:
Rather than offering a polite platitude, this observation challenges how we navigate our inner lives. True art and creative work are not about clever technique; they demand total emotional skin in the game. When you create safely to please an audience or avoid criticism, the work feels hollow and bloodless.

In Leonardo da Vinci's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. Pouring your genuine spirit, vulnerability, and raw lived experience into what you make is what gives it enduring life. The work that resonates across centuries is always the work created with unapologetic personal truth.
reflectionPrompt: How can you welcome mistakes and awkward beginnings as essential steps in your creative evolution?
